thought.text: Docling container started. The Keycloak login test hit that intermittent podman hijack again. Let me retry it alone:

reasoning_content:
The docling container started up. But the keycloak login test command threw that podman error again — weird. Something in my command is triggering it. Let me look: the command contains `sed -E 's/^/export /'` — no wait... the error "Cannot connect to Podman" is appearing for some of my commands. Let me figure out which part is triggering it.

No wait — could it be that the `docker run` in the first parallel command somehow set up something... no, that's not it. Let me re-run the keycloak test on its own and see if it works.

The podman error is happening intermittently. It's probably being caused by some command substitution or the curl to keycloak... Actually, looking more carefully: "read tcp 127.0.0.1:61421->127.0.0.1:59571" — port 59571 is the podman connection. Something in the environment is hooking into certain commands.

Let me retry the keycloak login on its own.

action.command:
cd /workspace
eval $(grep -E "^(LOCAL_USER_EMAIL|LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD)=" .env | sed 's/^/export /')
echo "user: $LOCAL_USER_EMAIL"
JAR=/tmp/kc-cookies.txt; rm -f $JAR
curl -sS -c $JAR -o /tmp/kc-login.html -w "auth-url: %{http_code}\n" "http://localhost:9090/realms/local/protocol/openid-connect/auth?client_id=local-client&redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000/oauth2/callback&response_type=code&scope=openid&state=teststate"
